description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for hyperscale data centres.
source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with large hyperscale facilities potentially as low as 1.1. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports low hyperscale PUE assumptions.

description: Facility-level annual load factor for hyperscale data centres, defined as average realised grid-side load divided by reported or estimated grid-side/nameplate capacity.
source: EPRI 2026; observed large hyperscale facility annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 used only as supporting evidence on high relative hyperscale server operational time.

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for hyperscale AI data centres.
source: EPRI 2026; large hyperscale facilities with liquid cooling may reach PUE as low as 1.1. Shehabi et al. 2024 models AI data centres separately by cooling system.

description: Facility-level annual load factor for hyperscale data centres with substantial AI workloads. Treated as high-utilisation but not full nameplate operation.
source: EPRI 2026; hyperscale observed annual load factor of 75% relative to nameplate capacity. Shehabi et al. 2024 distinguishes AI training and inference operational time. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes AI training is relatively flat while inference is peakier.

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for AI/HPC-oriented facilities.
source: Shehabi et al. 2024; AI data centres modelled separately for air and liquid cooling. EPRI 2026 supports lower PUE for newer large facilities.

description: Facility-level annual load factor for AI/HPC-oriented facilities, interpreted as training- or batch-compute-dominated.
source: Shehabi et al. 2024; AI training server operational time assumed at 80%, varied between 75-85%. EPRI 2026 provides facility-level support that hyperscale load factors can be high but below nameplate.

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for colocation facilities with AI workloads.
source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with older/smaller facilities higher. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports colocation PUE below roughly 1.4 in recent years.

description: Facility-level annual load factor for colocation facilities with AI-oriented workloads. Set above conventional colocation due to AI/HPC tenants, but below dedicated hyperscale or AI/HPC facilities.
source: EPRI 2026; smaller multi-tenant co-location facilities averaged 57% annual load factor relative to nameplate. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 notes colocation load is relatively consistent due to tenant diversity, while AI workloads may increase variability.

description: Power Usage Effectiveness assumed for colocation facilities.
source: EPRI 2026; average U.S. data centre PUE estimated at 1.32 in 2024, with older/smaller facilities higher. Shehabi et al. 2024 supports colocation PUE below roughly 1.4 in recent years.

description: Facility-level annual load factor for conventional multi-tenant colocation facilities, defined relative to reported or estimated grid-side/nameplate capacity.
source: EPRI 2026; smaller multi-tenant co-location facilities averaged 57% annual load factor relative to nameplate capacity. Regen/National Grid DSO 2025 supports relatively consistent colocation load due to flat storage/cloud use cases and tenant diversity.

description: Placeholder Power Usage Effectiveness for research/SMR-linked concept entries if an IT-load estimate is later specified.
source: Placeholder aligned with AI/HPC-oriented facilities. Concept entries are not translated into grid-side load unless IT load is specified.

description: Placeholder facility-level annual load factor for research/SMR-linked concept entries if an IT-load or grid-side load estimate is later specified.
source: Placeholder aligned with AI/HPC-oriented facilities. Concept entries are not translated into annual electricity use unless IT/grid-side load is specified.
